title: VPC audit log shipper Terraform module: CloudTrail -> S3 -> OpenSearch with retention + health checks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module for shipping VPC audit logs (CloudTrail) into a hardened auditing pipeline that stores raw events in an S3 account, applies lifecycle/GLACIER rules, and indexes transformed records into a dedicated OpenSearch domain. The module must support cross-account log ingestion, optional KMS encryption with customer-managed keys, configurable ILM/lifecycle policies, and automated deployment health checks suitable for Private (VPC) deployments. This is intended for Redwood Private customers who require auditable, durable log retention and queryability without exposing internal VPC networks.
scope: Terraform module that provisions: CloudTrail log bucket (cross-account), S3 bucket lifecycle rules, S3 notification -> shipper (Fargate or Lambda opt-out), OpenSearch domain + index templates, ILM/policy templates, KMS key resources (optional CMK)

Shipper implementation choices: containerized shipper deployed in customer VPC as Fargate/ECS task (default) with IAM role chaining for cross-account access; Lambda option kept for low-throughput dev use-cases
Health checks: CloudWatch alarms for delivery failures, custom synthetic OpenSearch query health job, and a terraform-driven 'canary' that writes/reads one event post-deploy
Upgrade strategy: in-place index template updates + controlled index rollover; major OpenSearch version upgrades via blue/green domain replacement with automated reindex job
Operational runbooks: automated recovery to fall back to raw S3 read model if OpenSearch becomes unavailable
acceptance_criteria: Module can be instantiated in a customer VPC with minimal variables to enable end-to-end ingestion (CloudTrail -> S3 -> shipper -> OpenSearch)
S3 lifecycle configured to move logs to Glacier/Deep archive after configurable days and enforce versioning/encryption
OpenSearch domain deployed inside customer's VPC with index templates and ILM policies that match retention requirements
Healthcheck suite runs as part of terraform apply: writes a single event to S3 and verifies it appears searchable in OpenSearch within configured SLA
Cross-account KMS key options tested: account-owned CMK and customer-provided key both supported
Module has CI validation: terraform fmt/validate, unit tests for plan comparisons, and an integration test harness that runs against a sandbox AWS account
risks_and_tradeoffs: Using Fargate shipper increases cost vs. Lambda for small volumes but avoids cold-starts and offers more predictable throughput for larger enterprise customers
Blue/green OpenSearch upgrades require temporary extra capacity and a reindex step; accepted in exchange for minimal downtime and data integrity guarantees
Cross-account encryption adds complexity around KMS grants and key rotation; documentation and an automation script will be provided to simplify grant management
Relying on S3 notifications to trigger shipper requires robust retry semantics; we'll implement idempotent processing and a dead-letter S3 prefix for failed batches
implementation_notes: Prefer modular TF structure: modules/logging-s3, modules/logging-shipper, modules/opensearch-indexing, modules/kms. Each module exposes small, testable inputs/outputs.
Shipper: Golang service with S3 consumer + bulk OpenSearch writer, exposes /health and /metrics endpoints. Defaults to ECS/Fargate using awsvpc networking inside the customer's subnet.

Healthchecks: terraform creates a 'deploy-canary' Step Function that writes a JSON event to S3 and polls OpenSearch until searchable or timeout. Failure surfaces as a terraform apply error if canary_required=true.
Testing: integration tests will run in CI on a dedicated sandbox account; use temporary credentials and destroy resources after tests to control cost.
Docs: Author Confluence runbook for KMS grants, key rotation, and troubleshooting shipper errors. Include example CRs for enterprise compliance audits.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Miguel Santos: Initial design review complete. Decided to default to Fargate shipper for customer scale; Lambda remains as an opt-in flag. See design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/15432/VPC+Audit+Shipper+Design
2026-02-27 - Asha Patel: Prototype shipper container built, local integration with OpenSearch v1.3 works. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4021
2026-03-03 - Security review request filed. Noted need for explicit KMS grant automation for cross-account ingest. Security suggested using least-privilege role assumption and short-lived sessions.
2026-03-08 - Miguel Santos: Implemented canary Step Function and terraform null_resource that triggers the canary post-apply. Still iterating on timeout behavior (current default 60s).

2026-03-11 - QA: Found intermittent S3 notification duplication causing duplicate indexed documents. Mitigation: shipper now deduplicates by S3 object etag + event time. Added DLQ handling to S3 notification config.

upgrade_strategy: Minor template/ILM updates: patch via terraform apply with index template versioning; old indices remain searchable
OpenSearch minor upgrades: rolling upgrade with reindex where necessary using a new domain and reindex-from-remote into the new cluster
Module config changes that are destructive will require explicit approval flag (force_replace=true) and will run in a preview sandbox before production rollout
monitoring_and_alerting: CloudWatch alarms for S3 delivery errors, ECS task failures, and OpenSearch cluster status
Prometheus metrics from shipper exported to CloudWatch Agent and visible in Redwood Console under private deployments
Synthetic check: periodic search query that validates the most-recent canary event is returned within SLA
